slides.text: Enterprise AI tools can cost six thousand pounds a year
slides.voiceover_text: Did you know an enterprise AI assistant can cost a small team six thousand pounds a year?

slides.text: Track where your team's time actually disappears first
slides.voiceover_text: Tip one: track where your team's time actually disappears before you assume AI is the fix.

slides.text: Check the tool fits your existing software stack
slides.voiceover_text: Tip two: check any tool fits your existing software stack, not just one part of it.

slides.text: Try a simple chatbot before an enterprise platform
slides.voiceover_text: Tip three: try a simple chatbot or template first, before an expensive enterprise platform.

slides.text: Simple tools often beat expensive ones
slides.voiceover_text: So remember: simple, focused tools often beat the expensive enterprise platform.

geo_answer: Most UK SMEs do not need enterprise AI workplace assistants like Copilot or Agentforce; simpler, focused automation often delivers most of the value at a fraction of the cost.
geo_takeaways: Enterprise AI assistants such as Microsoft Copilot cost around £30 per user monthly, on top of existing subscriptions.
A 10-person business can expect to pay £3,600 to £6,000 or more a year for an enterprise AI assistant.
Justifying that cost typically needs around 30 minutes of genuine time savings per employee per day.
Simpler alternatives, such as website chatbots and basic workflow automation, can deliver about 80% of the value at 20% of the cost.
